learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle. Both halves match perfectly! That fold is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many, and some have none.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A triangle with all sides equal has 3 lines of symmetry. A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Letters like A, T and V have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry. B, C and E have a lying (horizontal) one. F, L, N and S have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Fold H from top to bottom down the middle: the halves match.
Fold H from left to right across the middle: the halves match.
No other fold works.

learn.reallife: Rangoli, the Taj Mahal from the front, leaves and many logos are symmetrical.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded in half 4 ways: up-down, left-right and along both corner-to-corner lines.
steps: A line of symmetry is a fold where both halves match exactly.
A square folds evenly up-down, left-right, and along both corner-to-corner lines.
That is 2 + 2 = 4 lines of symmetry.
Answer: 4

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: It folds evenly only across the middle in two ways. A corner-to-corner fold does not make the halves match.
steps: Fold a rectangle across the middle and along the middle: both halves match.
Fold it corner to corner: the halves do not match.
So a rectangle (not a square) has 2 lines of symmetry.
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry, like in a square

quiz.q: Which letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A folds down the middle into two matching halves. F, L and N do not match when folded.
steps: Fold each letter down the middle and check if the halves match.
A: the left and right halves match.
F, L and N do not match when folded, so the answer is A.
Answer: A
quiz.mistake: Thinks any letter with straight lines is symmetrical

quiz.q: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes the two halves of S match. H, T and E each have at least one line of symmetry.
steps: H, T and E each fold into matching halves (at least one way).
No fold makes the two halves of S match.
Looking the same upside down is a turn, not a fold. So S has no line of symmetry.
Answer: S
quiz.mistake: Thinks S is symmetrical because it looks the same when turned upside down

quiz.q: A triangle has all 3 sides equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: You can fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That is 3 lines.
steps: Fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
Each of these folds makes matching halves.
There are 3 corners, so 3 lines of symmetry.
Answer: 3

quiz.q: Which letter has a lying (horizontal) line of symmetry, so its top half matches its bottom half?
quiz.explain: B folded from top to bottom matches. A, T and V have only a standing line of symmetry.
steps: A lying line means folding the top half onto the bottom half.
B: its top and bottom bumps match.
A, T and V only have a standing line.
Answer: B
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
quiz.explain: H matches when folded down the middle and when folded across the middle. That is 2 lines.
steps: Fold H down the middle: the halves match (1 line).
Fold H across the middle: the top and bottom match (2nd line).
So H has 2 lines of symmetry.
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Finds only one of the two folds

quiz.q: Which of these has the most lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves, so a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
steps: Square: 4 lines. Rectangle: 2. Equal-sided triangle: 3.
Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves.
So a circle has endless lines, the most.
Answer: A circle
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square has the most because it has 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper heart down the middle and both halves matched! What is that fold line called?
teach.praise: Yes! When both halves match after folding, the fold is a line of symmetry. Gappu loves it!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when Gappu folds? What do we call that line?

revise.summary: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded. Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many and some have none.
focus: Count lines of symmetry of squares, rectangles, triangles and circles
Find letters with standing, lying or no lines of symmetry
remember: Square: 4 lines. Rectangle that is not a square: 2
Triangle with all sides equal: 3. Circle: endless
A, T, V: standing line. B, C, E: lying line. F, L, N, S: none
traps: Don't forget the two corner-to-corner folds of a square
The diagonals of a rectangle are not lines of symmetry
Don't mix up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

learn.hook: Drop some paint on paper, fold it, press and open. A butterfly appears! How?
points: Ink-blot design: put paint on one half, fold along the middle, press and open. The paint copies onto the other half like a mirror image.
The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design.
When folding a paper plane, the first middle fold is its line of symmetry. Both wings should match.
Place a mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture and you see the whole picture.
A symmetrical plane flies straighter. If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over.

example.q: Ritu folds a paper plane but one wing is bigger than the other. What will probably happen when she throws it?
steps: The plane is not symmetrical.
One side pushes on the air more than the other.
So the plane turns or tips instead of flying straight.
example.answer: It will turn or tip to one side

learn.reallife: Rangoli artists, ink-blot painters and paper-plane champions all use a fold line to make matching halves.

The mirror shows the missing half.

It is a mirror image, flipped left to right.
The middle fold of a paper plane helps make both wings equal.
It is the plane's line of symmetry.

quiz.q: In an ink-blot design, what is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: The fold line splits the design into two matching halves.
steps: The fold splits the ink-blot design into two matching halves.
A line that makes matching halves is a line of symmetry.
So the fold line is the line of symmetry.
Answer: Line of symmetry

quiz.q: Paint is put on the left half and the paper is folded. Where does the copy appear?
options: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.explain: Folding presses the paint onto the other half as a mirror image.
steps: Folding presses the paint from the left half onto the right half.
The copy is a mirror image.
So it appears on the right half, flipped like a mirror.
Answer: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.mistake: Thinks the copy is not flipped

quiz.q: Why should both wings of a paper plane be the same?
quiz.explain: A symmetrical plane balances and flies straight.
steps: If both wings are the same, the plane is balanced.
A balanced (symmetrical) plane does not pull to one side.
So it flies straight.
Answer: So it flies straight
quiz.mistake: Does not link symmetry to balance

quiz.q: Which fold is the line of symmetry of a paper plane?
options: The first fold down the middle
A fold at one wing tip

steps: A line of symmetry splits the plane into two equal halves.
The first fold down the middle does exactly this.
A fold at a wing tip or the nose is not in the middle.
Answer: The first fold down the middle
quiz.mistake: Picks a fold that is not in the middle

quiz.q: Ankit places a mirror along the middle of half a butterfly drawing. What does he see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the other matching half, so the whole butterfly appears.
steps: A mirror on the line of symmetry shows the matching half.
Half a butterfly + its mirror half = a whole butterfly.
So Ankit sees a whole butterfly.
Answer: A whole butterfly
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a mirror shows

quiz.q: An ink-blot design has 6 dots on the left half before folding (none on the fold). How many dots after opening?
quiz.explain: Each dot is copied to the right half: 6 + 6 = 12.
steps: Folding copies each dot onto the right half.
Left 6 dots + right 6 dots.
Answer: 12

quiz.q: A plane drifts to the left every time. What is likely wrong?
quiz.explain: Unequal (not symmetrical) wings make a plane turn.
steps: A symmetrical plane flies straight.
If it always drifts one way, its two sides are not the same.
So the wings are not equal.
Answer: The wings are not equal

quiz.q: A mirror is placed on the line of symmetry of half the letter A. What letter do you see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the missing half, completing the A.
steps: A has a standing line of symmetry down the middle.
A mirror on that line shows the missing half.
Together they make the whole letter A.
Answer: A
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror shows a different letter

teach.nudge: What does folding do to the paint on one half?

revise.summary: In an ink-blot design, paint on one half copies onto the other half as a mirror image, and the fold line is the line of symmetry. A symmetrical paper plane with matching wings flies straighter.

Find the line of symmetry of a paper plane
Use a mirror to complete half a picture
remember: The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design
A mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture shows the whole picture
If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over

learn.hook: Put a mirror on half a picture and, like magic, the whole picture appears!
points: A mirror shows a flipped copy. Left becomes right and right becomes left.
If you know one half of a symmetrical shape, you can draw the other half like a mirror image.
Each point on one side is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner on the other side.
Fold paper, cut a shape on the fold and open it. You get a symmetrical shape!
In a mirror, b looks like d.

steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.

Cutting half a heart on the fold cuts both layers at once.

quiz.q: In a mirror held to its side, what does the letter b look like?

The bump of b is on the right; in the mirror it moves to the left.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: M and O look the same when flipped, and MOM reads the same both ways. B, D, S, N and P do not.
steps: A word stays the same in a side mirror if each letter is symmetrical and the word reads the same both ways.
M and O are symmetrical, and MOM reads the same backwards.
B, D, S, N and P flip, so the answer is MOM.
Answer: MOM
quiz.mistake: Checks only one letter of the word

quiz.q: Which digit looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: 8 has a standing line of symmetry, so its mirror image is the same. 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.
steps: A side mirror flips left and right.
8 has a standing line of symmetry, so it looks the same.
2, 4 and 7 face the other way in a mirror.
Answer: The digit 8

topics.title: Holes and cuts: predict the pattern

learn.hook: Fold a paper twice, snip a corner, and open it. Will you get one hole or four?
points: Folding once makes 2 layers. A cut away from the fold makes 2 holes; a cut on the fold makes 1 hole.
Folding twice makes 4 layers. A cut in the middle (away from all folds) makes 4 holes.
A cut at the corner where both folds meet makes 1 hole in the centre of the paper.
A cut on just one folded edge (not the corner) makes 2 holes.
To get a square hole, fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner, the same distance along both folds.

example.q: A paper is folded twice. A small half-circle is cut on one folded edge, away from the corner. How many holes after opening?
steps: Folded twice means 4 layers.
On a fold, the 4 layers pair up into 2 holes.
So there are 2 holes.

learn.reallife: Paper snowflakes and paper lanterns for Diwali are made by folding and cutting. The more folds, the more holes!

games.title: Predict the cut

2, 4, then 8 layers.

The two halves join into 1 circle hole.
Answer: 1 circle hole

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a small hole punched away from the fold. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.
steps: A paper folded once has 2 layers.
A punch away from the fold goes through both layers.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a hole punched in the middle, away from all folds. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so 4 holes.
steps: 2 folds → 4 layers
4 holes
Answer: 4

quiz.q: A paper is folded twice and a quarter circle is cut at the corner where both folds meet. What do you get?
quiz.explain: The 4 quarter circles join into one circle in the middle.
steps: Folding twice makes 4 layers that meet at the folded corner.
The quarter circle at that corner is copied into 4 quarters.
The 4 quarters join into 1 circle in the centre.
Answer: 1 circle in the centre
quiz.mistake: Thinks each layer gives a separate hole

quiz.q: How many layers are there after folding a paper 3 times?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, 4, 8.
steps: Each fold doubles the layers.
1 fold: 2, 2 folds: 4, 3 folds: 8.
2 × 2 × 2 = 8 layers.
Answer: 8

quiz.q: Maya wants a square hole in the centre. What should she do?
options: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner
Fold once and cut a circle

steps: To get one hole in the centre, cut at the corner where the folds meet.
Fold twice, then cut straight across the folded corner.
The 4 small triangles open into one square hole.
Answer: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner

quiz.q: A paper is folded once. On the fold, Ravi cuts a rectangle 1 cm wide (from the fold) and 2 cm long (along the fold). What hole does he get?
quiz.explain: The 1 cm width doubles to 2 cm when opened, so the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.
steps: The rectangle is cut on the fold, so its width doubles when opened.
1 cm from the fold → 1 + 1 = 2 cm wide. Length along the fold stays 2 cm.
So the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.
Answer: A 2 cm by 2 cm square

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a small notch cut on one folded edge, not at the corner. How many notches or holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The 4 layers pair up across the fold, making 2 holes.
steps: Folding twice makes 4 layers.
A notch on a folded edge cuts layers in pairs that are joined across that fold.
4 layers ÷ 2 = 2 holes.
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Thinks every cut on 4 layers gives 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded paper twice and punched one hole in the middle. Gappu expected 1 hole but got 4. Explain.
teach.praise: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes! Now I can predict.

learn.hook: The word AMBULANCE is written back to front on the van. Why? Look in a car's mirror!
points: Place a mirror on a shape. If the shape and its reflection make the same shape, the mirror is on a line of symmetry.
Digits like 0, 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror held beside them.
A mirror also reverses the order of digits. So only numbers like 88, 101 and 808 look the same in the mirror.
AMBULANCE is written in mirror writing on the front of the van so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirror.
You can try mirror writing in any script: write each letter flipped, starting from the other side.

example.q: Does 18 look the same in a mirror held beside it?
steps: 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror.
But the mirror swaps their order: 18 looks like 81.
So 18 does not look the same.

learn.reallife: Next time you see an ambulance, look at the front. The writing is reversed for the mirrors of cars in front!

topics.title: Symmetry of regular shapes on a dot grid

learn.hook: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry. Coincidence? Let's check other shapes!
points: A regular shape has all sides equal and all angles equal.
Regular triangle: 3 lines of symmetry. Square: 4. Regular pentagon: 5. Regular hexagon: 6.
For a regular shape, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2. A shape like a kite has 1.
On a dot grid, draw a shape and then test each possible fold line to find its lines of symmetry.

example.q: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
steps: For a regular shape, lines = sides.
So 6 lines of symmetry.

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, road signs and honeycombs often use regular shapes because they look balanced from every side.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
quiz.explain: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry.
steps: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.
A regular pentagon has 5 sides.
So it has 5 lines of symmetry.
Answer: 5

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
quiz.explain: Regular shapes have as many lines of symmetry as sides.
steps: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.
A regular hexagon has 6 sides.
So 6 lines (3 through corners, 3 through middles of sides).
Answer: 6

quiz.q: A square has 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?

learn.hook: Cut a bump from one side of a square and stick it on the opposite side. You get a cat-shaped tile that still fits!
points: A floor pattern is made by repeating one tessellating tile again and again.
Catty-wall trick: cut a piece from one side of a square and slide it to the opposite side.
The new tile has a funny shape (like a cat), but copies still fit together with no gaps.
The area stays the same, because nothing was thrown away: the piece only moved.
If the piece is not slid exactly to the opposite side, the tiles will not fit.

example.q: Raghav cuts a small triangle from the bottom of a square tile and sticks it on the top. Will copies fit together?
steps: The bump on top matches the gap at the bottom of the tile above.
So copies fit with no gaps or overlaps.
